newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: DRB-Hicom plans large investment in waste disposal.
newsitem.headline: DRB-Hicom plans large investment in waste disposal.

text.p: Malaysian automobile, finance and construction group DRB-Hicom said it has been given waste disposal contracts for five states, which will require a multi-billion dollar investment.

The group's chairman Saleh Sulong told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday that the government has given DRB-Hicom the contract for the federal territory of Kuala Lumpur, and states of Selangor, Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan.
"It will require a multi-billion dollar investment," he said. "An incineration plant capable of handling 3,000 tonnes of waste per day may cost as much as 1.5 billion ringgit per day," he noted.
"As of now, we are handling Kuala Lumpur for most parts of the city. We are continuing very much the way it was done before," he said.
But, the group was considering various alternatives to the present landfill method for the disposal of the waste, Saleh said.
He said the investment will be made over an extended period.
